design_concepts.name: Clinical Command Grid
design_concepts.direction: High-clarity Swiss operations board with warm paper-white surfaces, visible grid skeleton, rust action accents, and compact chair lanes.

design_concepts.name: Paper Diary Rebuilt
design_concepts.direction: Digital translation of a trusted paper diary: ruled time columns, ink-like labels, marginal date notes, and tactile status marks without skeuomorphic clutter.

design_concepts.name: Quiet Triage
design_concepts.direction: Monochrome scheduling canvas with one signal color reserved for conflicts and one arrival color for flow; strong hierarchy for reception speed.

design_concepts.name: Chair Atlas
design_concepts.direction: Nine-chair matrix treated like a spatial map, with drill-down rail, chair identity chips, and an understated architectural coordinate system.

design_concepts.name: Shift Ledger
design_concepts.direction: Editorial operations dashboard using serif date typography, mono time labels, and dense but breathable ledger rows for doctor-heavy scheduling.

selected_direction.name: Clinical Command Grid
selected_direction.rationale: The tool is used by reception and doctors during live operations. A light, cardless, high-density grid makes all 9 chairs scannable at once while warm neutrals prevent the cold hospital-template feeling. The paper-diary reference is fused with Swiss information design and architectural wayfinding.
selected_direction.breaks_pattern: The schedule is not a conventional centered calendar or collection of rounded cards. The live board occupies the visual center, while controls form a left utility rail and the right side remains an optional detail drawer; this creates operational tension and keeps the user's eye on time intersections.

rules: Use Manrope 650-800 for page and section headings; never use Inter for headings.
Use IBM Plex Sans for labels, forms, tables, and body copy.
Use IBM Plex Mono for time labels, chair IDs, booking IDs, and conflict messages.
H1 max text-4xl sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl; H2 max text-2xl sm:text-3xl lg:text-4xl.
Overlines are uppercase text-xs with tracking-[0.2em]. Headings use tracking-tight and leading-none; body uses leading-relaxed.

colors.archetype: Swiss & high-contrast with warm paper tint
rules: Use color as function only; 85-90% of UI stays neutral.
Never use pure black, pure gray, teal-blue, or full-screen gradients.
Primary rust is reserved for create booking and high-priority actions.
Status chips must include text, not color alone; verify at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
Use solid surfaces in the header and schedule; no complete transparent overlays.

layouts.app_shell: Desktop: fixed 248px solid left navigation rail, sticky 72px top utility header, schedule workspace. Tablet: collapsible rail and horizontal toolbar. Mobile: stacked day agenda with chair selector; do not attempt to shrink all 9 columns below usability.
layouts.primary_board: Use a high-density grid: grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-4 for summary/filter widgets, then a full-width schedule canvas. Schedule has a sticky chair-name column and horizontally scrollable time lanes. All 9 chairs remain simultaneously visible on desktop.
layouts.schedule_geometry: Rows are chairs, columns are configured intervals from 09:00 to 21:00. Use 30-minute default with 15/30/60 configurable. Booking blocks span their duration and show doctor plus patient name/ID.
layouts.right_drawer: Booking details/edit drawer opens from the right without losing board context. On mobile use a Shadcn Sheet.
layouts.spacing: Use p-6 and p-8 within bordered surfaces, gap-4 to gap-6 for dense dashboard widgets, and larger py-12 section separation. Avoid jagged bottoms with h-full and align-items:start.
layouts.grid_protocol: Use visible 1px grid borders, rectangular surfaces, max 8px radius. Do not overuse Card; use raw div/section for the board and Shadcn components for interactions.

component_path: /app/frontend/src/components/ (JavaScript .js/.jsx files only; do not create .tsx files)
interaction_rules: Use Shadcn Dialog, Sheet, Select, Calendar, DropdownMenu, Form, Input, and Sonner for interactions; never native select/date picker.
Create booking is a fast path: click empty slot, prefill chair/date/time, then choose doctor and enter patient name/ID and duration.
Conflict responses are server authoritative: show the conflicting chair/time and preserve entered data for correction.
Reschedule preserves cancelled history and creates the replacement booking atomically.
Use hover to elevate booking blocks, active press scale subtly, and explicit high-contrast focus rings.
Every button, link, input, menu, booking block, status, conflict message, date control, filter, and confirmation text must include a stable kebab-case data-testid.

principles: Micro-interactions only; prioritize speed over spectacle.
Stagger navigation and board entrance by 30-50ms.
Animate booking block transform and opacity, never transition all.
Use a brief pulse on a newly synced booking and a shake-free inline conflict alert.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling entrance, pulse, and transform animations.
motion.durations: 120-220ms for controls; 250-350ms for drawers and dialogs

visual_enhancers: Subtle warm grain/noise texture at very low opacity on the app shell, aria-hidden.
Thin architectural crosshair/date marker for current time.
Small paper-rule dividers and mono time labels to echo the diary without decorative clutter.
Customized scrollbar with no gutter; retain visible horizontal scrolling for the schedule.

requirements: Keyboard navigation across schedule cells and booking blocks; Enter opens editor, Escape closes overlays.
Use aria-labels for chair rows, time cells, filters, and status changes.
Do not rely on color for Booked, Patient Arrived, Completed, Cancelled, or No-show.
Focus ring must be visible against warm surfaces; conflict and success feedback must be announced.
Maintain 4.5:1 normal text contrast, 3:1 large text and controls, and test at 200% zoom.
accessibility.test_ids: Use role-based names such as schedule-date-next-button, chair-03-lane, booking-create-submit-button, booking-conflict-alert, booking-status-select, admin-user-save-button.

media.guidance: No stock photography is needed for this internal dashboard. Do not add placeholder image URLs, avatars, or decorative medical imagery. Use CSS geometry and icons only.

3d_libraries.decision: Clarity beats immersion for a live scheduling board. Do not add R3F, WebGL, or decorative particle systems.

Admin: manage chairs, users, clinic hours, interval settings
Doctor: update allowed status according to product policy

server_rules: validate clinic hours and configured interval
broadcast booking create/update/cancel/status events over native FastAPI WebSocket
re-check conflict on every write; client checks are advisory only

documentation_to_include: Architecture overview: React dashboard, FastAPI REST plus native WebSocket channel, MongoDB persistence.
MongoDB collection/schema notes for users, chairs, settings, bookings, and cancelled history.
Role/permission matrix and API endpoint list.
Demo accounts: admin/admin123, reception/reception123, doctor/doctor123; clearly mark these as development credentials only.
GENERAL UI UX DESIGN GUIDELINES: Prioritize usable MVP speed and clarity over decorative novelty.
Every page has visible navigation with brand, 3-5 links, and a primary action on desktop.
Never use a transparent header or transparent content surface over underlying content; use solid or opaque glass with blur and border.
Avoid generic centered layouts, uniform cards, excessive gradients, emoji icons, and Inter headings.
Use generous spacing, layered hierarchy, crisp borders, and explicit hover/active/focus states.
All key interactive and informational elements require data-testid attributes.
Do not build EMR, billing/payments, patient medical records, SMS/WhatsApp integrations, public self-booking, native mobile app, or multi-clinic support.
instructions_to_main_agent: Implement the selected Clinical Command Grid direction in the existing React/FastAPI project. Preserve the schedule as the dominant interaction, use existing Shadcn primitives for dialogs/forms/selects/sheets/toasts, and keep the board cardless and operational. Validate responsive desktop/tablet behavior, WebSocket refresh states, server conflict errors, permissions, and data-testid coverage before handoff.
